rules: Explicit user decisions take precedence over source variants and model preferences.
Translate into natural Brazilian Portuguese; adapt grammar, articles, capitalization and number to the sentence.
Use the longest applicable complete technique name before a shorter generic glossary term.
This glossary guides translation; do not apply blind substring search-and-replace.
Preserve every <...> engine token exactly, including <ryou>, colors and controller symbols. Preserve the multiplicity of %1, %2 and other numbered arguments.
Retain source character names and existing honorifics. Do not infer speaker identity from a name mentioned in dialogue.
Keep the original story knowledge. Do not inject later identities, relationships, titles or names such as Kurama where the source does not reveal them.
Original table neighbors are supporting linguistic context, not proof of scene order or speaker.
Do not turn source utterances into facts about their speaker; faithfully translate jokes, threats, mistakes and uncertainty.
Contextual terms require the specified sense. Needs-review terms are unresolved candidates, not locked output.
The supplied URLs document terminology decisions; all translation-critical preferences and conditions are included here without requiring the model to browse.
